chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Port-au-Prince: gors, coasting Model-Ts and colored pilots
summary: He describes Port-au-Prince's poverty, coasting taxis, and the strain of the Haitian pilots boarding the fruit-line ship.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: And I can remind you, that's the beginning of the hill at Port Au Prince... Their market is at the bottom of the hill. All around it's like a mountain, and all this housing surrounds, like, the valley which is the center(?) of the palace, see. You take a little cab in those days... Port Au Prince was poor, and thanks to the generosity of Uncle Sam, they help everybody else but people in their hemisphere they have never tried to... But anyway, the denomination of their money was a gor(?), they call it -- it's about 10 cents or

20 cents, and you pay so many gors(?). The little cars... They were antiquated Model-T Fords that they had in those days. They would go uphill by gas. As soon as they'd get up the hill, they shut the motor off, and if you want to come downtown again they'd just coast down. They always had a brake problem, I believe, because gas was so rare, you know, that they just couldn't afford it. They'd just coast down the hill to anywhere you wanted...
With no engine, I think that is rough on the brakes, isn't it.
You couldn't hold a conversation with the motor running. They turned it off right away.

That was around what, '31, '32...? It was a show. We went by the United Fruit line. And I can tell you, it was very embarrassing for that boat to pull up in the harbor of Port Au Prince at the time and have colored pilots board(?)... You could feel the strain, you know. It was very sad, you know, the whole... The currency was controlled by the Export-Import Bank, which deserves a lot of...you know, ...(?)... speculation by the proper people. It's terrible, all those South American...Guatemala and all those countries. Oh, it's terrible.
